headline: Boone and Crockett Club is born
summary: Roosevelt gathers fellow hunters, among them Elliott, cousin West and George Bird Grinnell, to found the Boone and Crockett Club, devoted to outdoor life, hunting and protecting big game. With Roosevelt as president, the club pledges to push for game laws and their enforcement. For the cold months the family settles into 689 Madison Avenue.

events.detail: Founding meeting of the Boone and Crockett Club
Elected president of the new club, which aims to protect large game
Takes Edith, Alice and Ted to winter quarters at 689 Madison Avenue

uncertain: Date approximate: the club grew out of a dinner Roosevelt hosted in New York in December 1887 and was formally organized early in 1888; the source's Sagamore Hill setting is doubtful.
